links.outcome: Readability (Gunning Fog Index) of ChatGPT responses to patient questions on hard flaccid syndrome
links.effect: Mean Gunning Fog Index 15.19 (SD 1.68) at baseline and 14.59 (SD 1.66) after 48 hours (P=.33), an upper high school to early college reading level.
links.quote: Overall readability remained stable between sessions, with mean Gunning Fog Index scores of 15.19 (SD 1.68) at baseline and 14.59 (SD 1.66) after 48 hours (P=.33), corresponding to an upper high school to early college reading level.

links.outcome: Short-term reproducibility of ChatGPT responses across repeated sessions 48 hours apart
links.effect: 87.5% (14/16) of responses received identical final accuracy classifications between sessions.
links.quote: Short-term reproducibility was substantial, with 87.5% (14/16) of responses receiving identical final accuracy classifications between sessions.

screen.reason: The study evaluates ChatGPT's accuracy, readability, and reproducibility on patient-generated questions about Hard Flaccid Syndrome, but does not test an organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
